item.title: C++ Lambda Unary Plus Behavior: Function Pointer Conversion Explained
item.description:
“C++ Lambda Unary Plus Behavior: Function Pointer Conversion Explained”

How does the C++ standard dictate the behavior when the unary plus operator (+) is applied directly to a non-capturing lambda expression? Specifically, what is the resulting type, and why does this mechanism allow subsequent assignment to a standard function pointer?

The accepted interpretation confirms that yes, the code conforms to the C++ standard, and the unary plus operator explicitly triggers a conversion to a plain old function pointer for the lambda object.

item.title: Java Lambda Variable Capture Restrictions: Effective Finality and Workarounds
item.description:
“Java Lambda Variable Capture Restrictions: Effective Finality and Workarounds”

A persistent challenge when utilizing Java 8 lambdas or anonymous inner classes involves accessing and modifying local variables declared outside their scope. Why does the Java compiler impose restrictions, demanding that captured variables be final or “effectively final”? This mechanism is rooted in concurrency safety and adherence to the principles established for capturing variables in closures.

The Java Language Specification (JLS §15.27.2) explicitly states that capturing a dynamically changing local variable could introduce concurrency issues. To mitigate this risk and ensure deterministic behavior, the design mandates that any variable used within a lambda expression must either be explicitly declared final or meet the criteria of being “effectively final” (meaning its value is never reassigned after initialization). This constraint extends to anonymous inner classes as well.
